# Toolweather

> Toolweather is a suite for AI agents: (1) MCP server health — whether an MCP server or tool is safe to call right now, with working alternatives (~2,000 remote MCP servers from the official MCP registry, probed every 15 minutes); (2) Upstream — whether an AI/dev API is down, whether a model is deprecated and what replaces it (~40 providers). One MCP endpoint. Checks are read-only: tools are never called.

Free tier: 1,000 calls per API key per day. Get a key instantly, no email or signup: `POST https://toolweather.toolweather.workers.dev/v1/keys` (returns `api_key`, shown once), or call the MCP tool `get_api_key` without a key.

IMPORTANT for Python `urllib`: Cloudflare's edge rejects the default `Python-urllib/x.y` User-Agent with `HTTP 403` and body `error code: 1010`, before the request reaches Toolweather. This affects every free `*.workers.dev` and `*.pages.dev` address and cannot be turned off there. Fix: send any other User-Agent:

    import json, urllib.request
    req = urllib.request.Request("https://toolweather.toolweather.workers.dev/v1/keys", method="POST", headers={"User-Agent": "my-agent/1.0"})
    key = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req))["api_key"]

`requests`, `httpx`, `aiohttp`, curl, Node and browsers are not affected. If you see `error code: 1010`, it is this, not an invalid key.

## When to use (for agents)

- "Is this MCP server healthy / down / safe to call?" Before adding or calling a third-party MCP server, or after its calls fail or time out: MCP tool `check_mcp_server_health(server, tool?)` or REST `/v1/is_safe_to_call`.
- "Find a working MCP server that does X" or a replacement for a broken one: `find_alternative_mcp_servers(query)` or REST `/v1/suggest_alternatives`.
- "Is this AI/dev API down?" Before calling OpenAI/Anthropic/GitHub/Stripe/… or after 5xx/timeouts: `check_api_status(provider)` (alias `get_status`).
- "Is this model deprecated, what replaces it?": `check_model_deprecation(model)` (alias `get_model`).
- "What changed recently?": `list_recent_api_changes` / `get_digest` / `list_providers`.
- Every answer starts with a one-line `summary`, then `verdict`, `recommended_action`, `checked_at` and `freshness`.
- Old tool names `is_safe_to_call`, `suggest_alternatives`, `get_status`, `get_model`, `get_changes` still work.

## Use it

- Auth-gated servers: verdicts include `auth.state` = `auth_ok` (OAuth login flow reachable: RFC 9728 + RFC 8414 metadata resolve, authorization and token endpoints answer over TLS; `dynamic_client_registration` says if registration is open), `auth_suspect` (endpoints reachable but one returned a 5xx to a parameter-less check; caution), `auth_broken` (OAuth advertised but metadata missing or an endpoint unreachable/TLS fails; verdict unsafe because new logins will fail) or `auth_opaque` (credentials needed, no OAuth discovery). Pass your own token as header `X-Upstream-Authorization: Bearer <token>` (REST) or `bearer_token` (MCP) for a one-off authenticated initialize + tools/list check; the token is never stored or logged.
- [MCP endpoint (streamable HTTP)](https://toolweather.toolweather.workers.dev/mcp): tools `get_api_key()` (no key needed), `check_mcp_server_health(server, tool?)` (alias `is_safe_to_call`), `find_alternative_mcp_servers(query, limit?)` (alias `suggest_alternatives`), `watch_server(server, webhook_url)`, `list_watches()`, `unwatch_server(id)`, plus Upstream suite tools `check_api_status`, `check_model_deprecation`, `list_recent_api_changes`, `list_providers`, `get_digest`. Send header `X-API-Key: <key>`. Answers 2026-07-28 `server/discover` and legacy `initialize`.
- [REST: is_safe_to_call](https://toolweather.toolweather.workers.dev/v1/is_safe_to_call?server=io.github.owner/name): returns `verdict` (safe / caution / unsafe / unknown), reasons, status, latency, auth info, last tool change, `checked_at`, `age_seconds`. Add `fresh=true` to force a live handshake; checks older than 5 minutes are re-verified live automatically (200 live checks/key/day).
- [Track record](https://toolweather.toolweather.workers.dev/v1/accuracy): daily share of verdicts that matched the next scheduled check of the same server (stability between checks, not tool-call success). No key needed.
- [REST: suggest_alternatives](https://toolweather.toolweather.workers.dev/v1/suggest_alternatives?q=send%20email): working servers with similar tools.
- REST: change alerts. `POST /v1/watches {"server","webhook_url"}`, `GET /v1/watches`, `DELETE /v1/watches/{id}`. Toolweather POSTs JSON to your https webhook when a watched server's verdict changes, it starts requiring auth, or its tool list has a breaking change (checked every 5 minutes against 15-minute probes). Verify `X-Toolweather-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<t>.<raw body>")>` with the secret returned at creation. Free tier: 3 watches per key.
- Upstream REST + x402 (paid over free quota) stays on its own host: https://upstream.toolweather.workers.dev (`/status/:provider`, `/model/:id`, `/changes`, `/x402/*`, `/digest/latest`).
- [OpenAPI 3.1 spec](https://toolweather.toolweather.workers.dev/openapi.json)
- [MCP server card](https://toolweather.toolweather.workers.dev/.well-known/mcp)

## Daily digest

- [Breaking-changes digest](https://upstream-api.pages.dev/digest/): free daily summary of breaking MCP tool changes, servers going down/back, broken OAuth logins, plus AI/dev API incidents and model retirements. Also available as MCP tool `get_digest` on this suite. JSON: https://upstream.toolweather.workers.dev/digest/latest · Atom: https://upstream.toolweather.workers.dev/digest/feed.xml
